# ffcc-gci usage

ffcc-gci is a save editor for Final Fantasy Crystal Chronicles (GameCube, PAL).

This page lists every command, flag and accepted value. The program prints the same information with `ffcc-gci help -all`, and the help of one command with `ffcc-gci help <command>`.

## Before you start

- Only saves of the European (PAL) version of the game are supported. Others are refused.
- Close Dolphin, or at least stop the game, before editing. Dolphin keeps the save in memory while a game runs and writes it back, which would undo the edit.
- The save Dolphin uses is a .gci file in its GCI folder, usually GC/EUR/Card A/ inside Dolphin's user directory.
- An edit in place first copies the original to \<save.gci\>.\<date-time\>.bak. To undo an edit, copy that backup back over the save.

## Commands

| Command | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`menu`](#menu) | Edit a save by answering questions instead of typing flags. |
| [`info`](#info) | Show the slots and characters of a save file. |
| [`set-gil`](#set-gil) | Set a character's gil. |
| [`add-artifact`](#add-artifact) | Grant a character an artifact. |
| [`artifacts`](#artifacts) | List the artifacts that can be granted. |
| [`add-item`](#add-item) | Add an item to a character's inventory. |
| [`items`](#items) | List the items that can be added. |
| [`limits`](#limits) | Show every editable value and its allowed range. |
| [`help`](#help) | Show help for the program or for one command. |
| [`version`](#version) | Print the program version. |

Flags can be written before or after the save file, and with one dash or two (`-slot` or `--slot`).

### menu

Edit a save by answering questions instead of typing flags.

```sh
ffcc-gci menu [save.gci]
```

The menu asks which slot and character to edit and what to change: the gil, an artifact or an item. It lists only what that character can receive, and typing narrows a long list down. Esc goes back one step and Ctrl+C quits.

The menu changes nothing by itself. For each edit it shows the set-gil, add-artifact or add-item command that does the same, asks for confirmation and runs that command. The edit is therefore checked and backed up exactly as one made with flags. To write to a new file with -o, use those commands.

Without a save file, the menu offers the saves it finds in Dolphin's European memory card folders, GC/EUR/Card A and Card B, or lets you browse for a file.

The menu is part of the program and needs nothing else installed. It has to run in a terminal: in a script, use the other commands.

Close Dolphin before editing: it rewrites the save while a game runs.

Examples:

```sh
# Edit a save through the menu
ffcc-gci menu save.gci

# Let the menu find the save in Dolphin's folders
ffcc-gci menu
```

### info

Show the slots and characters of a save file.

```sh
ffcc-gci info <save.gci>
```

Nothing is modified. For each of the four save slots it prints the town, the play time and every character with gil, hearts, stats, items and artifacts. The numbers it prints for slots and characters are the ones -slot and -char take.

Examples:

```sh
# Look at a save
ffcc-gci info save.gci
```

### set-gil

Set a character's gil.

```sh
ffcc-gci set-gil -slot <1-4> -char <name or 1-8> -gil <amount> [-o <new file>] <save.gci>
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-slot <1-4>` | Save slot to edit, as numbered by "ffcc-gci info". |
| `-char <name or 1-8>` | Character to edit: the name, or the number "ffcc-gci info" shows. |
| `-gil <amount>` | New amount of gil, 0 to 99999999. This is the range the game itself keeps gil in; anything outside it is refused. |
| `-o <new file>` | Write the result to this new file and leave the save untouched. |

Without -o the save is edited in place, and the original is first copied to a backup next to it, named \<save.gci\>.\<date-time\>.bak.

Close Dolphin before editing: it rewrites the save while a game runs.

Examples:

```sh
# Give Alba, in slot 3, 50000 gil
ffcc-gci set-gil -slot 3 -char Alba -gil 50000 save.gci

# Pick the character by number instead of by name
ffcc-gci set-gil -slot 3 -char 1 -gil 50000 save.gci

# Write a new file and leave the save untouched
ffcc-gci set-gil -slot 3 -char Alba -gil 50000 -o edited.gci save.gci
```

### add-artifact

Grant a character an artifact.

```sh
ffcc-gci add-artifact -slot <1-4> -char <name or 1-8> -artifact <name> [-o <new file>] <save.gci>
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-slot <1-4>` | Save slot to edit, as numbered by "ffcc-gci info". |
| `-char <name or 1-8>` | Character to edit: the name, or the number "ffcc-gci info" shows. |
| `-artifact <name>` | The artifact to grant: its name, a part of the name that matches only one artifact, or its item ID (159 to 231). "ffcc-gci artifacts" lists them all. |
| `-o <new file>` | Write the result to this new file and leave the save untouched. |

An artifact is either owned or not, so it cannot be granted twice: if the character already has it, nothing is written.

The game works out strength, magic, defence, hearts and command slots from the artifacts by itself, so the new values are there as soon as the save is loaded. "ffcc-gci info" reads the numbers the game last stored, and keeps showing the old ones until the game has saved again.

Without -o the save is edited in place, and the original is first copied to a backup next to it, named \<save.gci\>.\<date-time\>.bak.

Close Dolphin before editing: it rewrites the save while a game runs.

Examples:

```sh
# Grant an artifact by name
ffcc-gci add-artifact -slot 3 -char Alba -artifact "Sun Pendant" save.gci

# A part of the name is enough when it matches only one artifact
ffcc-gci add-artifact -slot 3 -char Alba -artifact kaiser save.gci

# Grant an artifact by item ID
ffcc-gci add-artifact -slot 3 -char Alba -artifact 231 save.gci
```

### artifacts

List the artifacts that can be granted.

```sh
ffcc-gci artifacts [text]
```

The artifacts are grouped by what they improve, each with its item ID and the game's description. With text, only artifacts whose name contains it are listed.

Examples:

```sh
# List every artifact
ffcc-gci artifacts

# List the artifacts with "ring" in the name
ffcc-gci artifacts ring
```

### add-item

Add an item to a character's inventory.

```sh
ffcc-gci add-item -slot <1-4> -char <name or 1-8> -item <name> [-count <n>] [-o <new file>] <save.gci>
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-slot <1-4>` | Save slot to edit, as numbered by "ffcc-gci info". |
| `-char <name or 1-8>` | Character to edit: the name, or the number "ffcc-gci info" shows. |
| `-item <name>` | The item to add: its name, a part of the name that matches only one item, or its item ID. "ffcc-gci items" lists what can be added; anything else is refused. |
| `-count <n>` | How many to add, 1 by default. Items do not stack: each one takes one of the character's 64 inventory slots, and the command refuses to add more than there are free slots. |
| `-o <new file>` | Write the result to this new file and leave the save untouched. |

Designs have two extra rules. A design is added only once, and only if it is for anyone or for the character's own tribe. Designs for men or for women are not supported.

Without -o the save is edited in place, and the original is first copied to a backup next to it, named \<save.gci\>.\<date-time\>.bak.

Close Dolphin before editing: it rewrites the save while a game runs.

Examples:

```sh
# Add one item
ffcc-gci add-item -slot 3 -char Alba -item Mythril save.gci

# Add several of the same item
ffcc-gci add-item -slot 3 -char Alba -item "Striped Apple" -count 5 save.gci

# Add a design
ffcc-gci add-item -slot 3 -char Alba -item "Iron Armour" save.gci

# Add an item by item ID
ffcc-gci add-item -slot 3 -char Alba -item 293 save.gci
```

### items

List the items that can be added.

```sh
ffcc-gci items [text]
```

The items are grouped as Phoenix Down, materials, food and designs, each with its item ID. With text, only items whose name contains it are listed.

Equipment, magicite, seeds, story items and unused entries of the game's item table are left out for safety and cannot be added.

Examples:

```sh
# List every item that can be added
ffcc-gci items

# List the items with "armour" in the name
ffcc-gci items armour
```

### limits

Show every editable value and its allowed range.

```sh
ffcc-gci limits
```

Each value the program can set has a fixed range taken from the game's own code. This prints every range and the reason it is safe.

Examples:

```sh
# Show the ranges
ffcc-gci limits
```

### help

Show help for the program or for one command.

```sh
ffcc-gci help [command | -all | -markdown]
```

| Flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `-all` | Print the help of every command, one after the other. |
| `-markdown` | Print the full reference in Markdown. docs/USAGE.md is this output. |

Without arguments it lists the commands. "ffcc-gci \<command\> -h" is the same as "ffcc-gci help \<command\>".

Examples:

```sh
# List the commands
ffcc-gci help

# Show the flags and examples of one command
ffcc-gci help add-item

# Show everything at once
ffcc-gci help -all
```

### version

Print the program version.

```sh
ffcc-gci version
```

It prints the version, the Go toolchain the program was built with and the platform, for example "ffcc-gci v1.0.0 (go1.27.3, linux/amd64)". A build that is not a release reports the version "dev" or the git revision.

Examples:

```sh
# Print the version
ffcc-gci version
```

## Exit codes

| Code | Meaning |
|---|---|
| 0 | The command succeeded. This includes an edit that was not needed, such as an artifact the character already has. |
| 1 | The command ran and failed, for example on an unsupported save or an empty slot. Nothing was written. |
| 2 | The command line was wrong: an unknown command, a missing flag or a value outside its range. Nothing was written. |

## Accepted values

Every value the program can set has a fixed range, taken from the game's own code. A value outside its range is refused and nothing is written. `ffcc-gci limits` prints this table.

| Value | Accepted range | Why it is safe |
|---|---|---|
| Gil | 0 to 99999999 | The game never lets gil leave this range: CCaravanWork::AddGil clamps to it and CCaravanWork::CanAddGil refuses to go past it (src/gobjwork.cpp). |
| Artifact item ID | 159 to 231 | These are the game's 73 artifacts. A character has a flag for each, and for 23 more item IDs that are unnamed placeholders and are refused (CMemoryCardMan::SetLoadData). A flag is on or off, so an artifact cannot be held twice. The game caps what artifacts add: strength, magic and defence at 99, hearts at 8, command slots at 8 (CCaravanWork::CalcStatus). |
| Phoenix Down item ID | 293 | The game describes this item as "Revives the fallen". Saves made by the game hold several at once. |
| Material item ID | 294 to 351 | The game describes each of these 58 items as "Material for equipment". The blacksmith counts how many of a material a character holds, so holding several of one is how the game is meant to work (SmithForgeScreen\_PrintNextRow in the GBA client). |
| Food item ID | 381 to 392 | The game describes each of these 12 items as "Restores HP" and its item menu puts them in one category (CMenuPcs::GetItemType). Saves made by the game hold several of one food. |
| Design item ID | 401 to 493 | The game describes each of these 93 items as a design, and all of them are working recipes in its item table. A character can be given a design only once, and only one for anyone or for the character's own tribe. |
| Items held by a character | 0 to 64 | A character has 64 inventory slots and the game refuses to add an item when all are used (CCaravanWork::AddItem). Items do not stack: each one takes a slot. |
| Slot | 1 to 4 | The slot must hold a save the game would load. Empty and damaged slots are refused. |
| Character | 1 to 8, or a name | The character must exist in the slot. Characters are never created. |
